claims.text: Only 9vHPV is available in the US; types 6 and 11 cause more than 90% of genital warts
claims.quote: Types 6 and 11 cause >90% of genital warts. Only 9vHPV vaccine is available in the United States.

claims.text: Routine at age 11 or 12 (can start at 9); catch-up through 26; shared decision-making for some unvaccinated adults 27 to 45
claims.quote: Routine HPV vaccination for all adolescents at age 11 or 12 years. Administering vaccine starting at age 9 years. Catch-up vaccination through age 26 years for those not vaccinated previously. Not using HPV vaccination for all adults aged >26 years. Instead, shared clinical decision-making between a patient and a provider regarding HPV vaccination is recommended for certain adults aged 27–45 years not vaccinated previously.

claims.text: 2 doses (0 and 6 to 12 months) if started before the 15th birthday; 3 doses (0, 1 to 2 and 6 months) for immunocompromised persons at any age
claims.quote: A 2-dose vaccine schedule (at 0- and 6–12-month intervals) is recommended for persons who initiate vaccination before their 15th birthday. A 3-dose vaccine schedule (at 0-, 1–2-, and 6-month intervals) for immunocompromised persons regardless of age of initiation.

claims.text: Not recommended in pregnancy; can be given regardless of a history of anogenital warts
claims.quote: HPV vaccines are not recommended for use in pregnant women. HPV vaccines can be administered regardless of history of anogenital warts
